title: Variables — practice quiz
description: A short check on what a variable is and how the four basic types work. This quiz does not run GDScript; it only checks that the ideas landed.

choices: Stores a piece of information the game can use and change later
questions.explain: A variable is a labeled box that holds a value, like the player's health or whether the flashlight is on. You can look at it or change it as the game runs.

questions.prompt: Which type should you use for `fear_level = 0.75`?
questions.explain: `0.75` has a decimal point, so it is a `float`. An `int` is only for whole numbers.

questions.prompt: Which line correctly makes a text variable?
questions.explain: Text values need quotes around them, and the line starts with `var`. Without quotes, Godot would think Basement is a name, not text.
A `bool` is a yes-or-no value. In GDScript that is just `true` or `false`, like whether the flashlight is on.
